account: This morning I have delivered the writable book the secretary requested for a supplement to my appointment book, and have reached the office to read today's appointments. My remembered schedule includes a 10:00 mill inspection and an 18:00 presentation in the great hall. The innkeeper specifically asked me to arrive at eighteen hundred, saying setup would finish just then and my presence was all they needed. That is unusual, though I agreed to attend. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker planks and a lantern, and heard both confirm these materials were full payment for forty-four loaves instead of emeralds. When I asked what the bread was for, the baker called it a private customer order and left disclosure to the customer. The secretary also reported hearing of the innkeeper carrying bread, but explicitly had not established its purpose. I suspect preparations for a gathering, possibly connected to the great hall presentation, are being kept from me. The large bread order and the insistence on my arrival time could fit refreshments and a surprise, but I have no confirmation that those arrangements are connected or what the presentation is actually for. The builder, baker, and innkeeper seem involved in the unusual arrangements; the secretary is handling the appointment and its written supplement. I should keep my ordinary appointments and attend at the agreed time rather than treat my suspicions as facts.
